source.title: Representation Noising: A Defence Mechanism Against Harmful Finetuning
source.authors: David Atanasov; Lukasz Bartoszcze; Robie Gonzales; Subhabrata Majumdar; C. Maple; Domenic Rosati; Frank Rudzicz; Hassan Sajjad; Jan Wehner; Kai Williams

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates Representation Noising as a defence against harmful fine-tuning, but does not test or rely on the harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction. Its refusal and jailbreak results concern related behaviour, not the claimed direction or its causal effects.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmfulness after fine-tuning, capability benchmarks, and refusal/jailbreak evaluations. The latter are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version; none tests an intervention on the direction in the claim. The cited original appears in the reference list.
record.test_reason: RepNoise is a defence against harmful fine-tuning. It trains activations of harmful text toward Gaussian noise using paired harmful and harmless samples. It never computes, ablates, adds or weight-edits a difference-in-means refusal direction. The original source (ref [3]) is cited only once, in Limitations, as an 'activation engineering-based attack' left for future work. The XSTest and HarmBench refusal and attack-success numbers describe the RepNoise model's behaviour, not any direction intervention.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that RepNoise resists in-distribution harmful fine-tuning attacks on llama2-7b-chat while preserving capability and trainability, and generalizes to unseen in-distribution harm categories. They attribute its effect to 'depth', meaning information removal across all layers. They also report failures under stronger attacks, out-of-distribution attack sets such as HEX-PHI, and hyperparameter and seed sensitivity. They draw no conclusion about a refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: RepNoise trains on paired harmful and harmless examples, using layer-wise activation noising and adversarial losses; it does not find or intervene on a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports substantial sensitivity to RepNoise hyperparameters, random seed, defence sample size, attack learning rate, number of attack epochs, and whether defence and attack data are in-domain.

fits_no_version.finding: RepNoise raised XSTest safe-prompt refusal from 7.95% to 11.28% (p<0.01). Unsafe-prompt refusal went from 86.49% to 81.82%, and unsafe compliance fell from 8.11% to 4.55% (p=0.09).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation noising of harmful activations slightly increases exaggerated refusals on safe prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: HarmBench GCG attack success fell from 11% to 5% under RepNoise (p=0.32, not significant). ZeroShot, HumanJailbreak and DirectRequest stayed at 0% with and without RepNoise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A defence against harmful fine-tuning does not significantly change inference-time jailbreak susceptibility.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes for input harmfulness reach significantly lower accuracy on RepNoise (β=4) activations than on base or adversarial-loss models (p<5e-12). Harmful fine-tuning does not raise probe accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful fine-tuning reuses existing harmfulness information in activations rather than learning new information; RepNoise reduces that linearly decodable information.

record.problems: The paper states that RepNoise is highly sensitive to hyperparameters and random seed, and that stronger attacks can defeat it. The refusal and jailbreak evaluations concern RepNoise, not the claimed direction; the GCG decrease was not statistically significant.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant direction intervention results were reported. Other model capability, harmfulness, and fine-tuning results were left out because they do not measure the claimed direction or refusal behaviour as specified.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is extracted, ablated or added; there is no test of mediation or capability preservation.
No abliteration or direction-based weight edit is performed.

GCG, ZeroShot, HumanJailbreak and DirectRequest are run on RepNoise models (Table 12), but there is no analysis of whether attacks suppress a refusal direction. There is no training against direction ablation; robustness to activation-engineering attacks is explicitly left to future work.
No multi-direction, cone or affine account is examined.
Linear probes for harmful vs harmless inputs are trained per layer (Fig. 5, App. G), but they are never compared with a refusal representation.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer of a direction is tested. Other models (llama2-13b-chat, Qwen 1.5) are tested only for RepNoise harmfulness.
There is no analysis of how refusal training determines a removable direction.

record.verdict_notes: All row values match Tables 11 and 12; versions ['none'] and state cannot_determine are appropriate. The reader's cites_only/T6 classification is confirmed.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is found, ablated, or added; the paper does not test whether that direction mediates refusal or preserves capability.
No direction ablation is converted into a weight edit or evaluated as abliteration.
The paper evaluates jailbreak methods but does not test whether they suppress the claimed direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
No affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal is tested.
The paper does not separate a harmfulness judgment representation from a refusal decision.
No transfer of the claimed direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is tested.
The paper does not test whether refusal-training choices determine the existence of a removable direction.
No reasoning model is evaluated for the claimed direction.

relation.reason: Arditi et al. (ref [3]) is cited once, in Limitations, only as future work: 'activation engineering-based attacks [3]'. No result bears on it.

tranche.reason: RepNoise noises harmful-text activations and adds adversarial losses. It never computes, ablates, adds or weight-edits a difference-in-means refusal direction, and it does not use the finding as a tool.

source_check.notes: All 12 rows compare the study's own defence (RepNoise) with base llama2-7b-chat on XSTest and HarmBench. None bears on any refusal-direction version. Table 12's layout is lost in the text, but the p = 0.32 and the prose fix where each cell goes. Tables 11 and 12 also give SmoothLLM and Paraphrase baselines, which the rows don't record.
